title: Emerging technologies are shifting value toward distributed infrastructure, point-of-use production, and personalized services while making trust and access central adoption constraints
source_unit: World Economic Forum, Top 10 Emerging Technologies of 2026, published with Frontiers and strategic outlook by Dubai Future Foundation
geography: Global technology, infrastructure, health, food, materials, and computing landscape

observations.period: June 2026; ten technologies selected for near-term potential impact

denominator.unit: technologies covered in the WEF report

technology_set.value: everything-to-grid energy; direct lithium extraction; passive radiative cooling; PFAS destruction; precision fermentation; exosome drug delivery; personalized mRNA cancer vaccines; quantum simulation for drug discovery; world models; lattice-based cryptography

deployment_orientation.value: the report frames the cohort as advances moving from research toward real-world deployment

observations.method: WEF publication developed with Frontiers and Dubai Future Foundation, using expert selection and qualitative technology assessment rather than a representative public survey or causal impact study.
observations.uncertainty: The cohort signals expert judgment about novelty, development progress, and potential impact; it does not estimate adoption probabilities, market size, public acceptance, or realized social outcomes.
observations.subgroup: Researchers, technology firms, utilities, manufacturers, hospitals, food producers, regulators, households, workers, and communities exposed to deployment choices.
observations.counterinterpretation: A technology can be technically promising yet fail to scale because of cost, regulation, infrastructure, supply chains, skills, liability, or public resistance; inclusion in a foresight list is not evidence of inevitability.

place_capability_decoupling.value: precision fermentation, direct lithium extraction, passive radiative cooling, and everything-to-grid are presented as technologies that can loosen the link between capability and traditional physical location

distributed_energy.value: buildings, vehicles, and devices can become active grid nodes that store, return, and coordinate electricity

food_production_shift.value: precision fermentation can produce proteins and other molecules where reliable power, feedstocks, and trained biologists are available rather than only where conventional agriculture supports them

observations.method: Qualitative synthesis of the report's technology descriptions and emerging-landscape discussion.
observations.uncertainty: The geographic effects depend on energy prices, capital, skills, local regulation, resource access, infrastructure, and whether production displaces or complements existing livelihoods.
observations.subgroup: Renters and homeowners, agricultural workers and regions, utilities, resource-producing communities, manufacturers, and local governments.
observations.counterinterpretation: Distributed or location-flexible production can diversify supply while concentrating control in software, finance, intellectual property, or specialized infrastructure owners.

value_location.value: the report identifies a shift from standardized mass production toward value produced closer to the point of use

personalized_oncology.value: personalized mRNA cancer vaccines use a patient's tumour mutations as the starting specification for therapy

biological_delivery.value: exosome drug delivery is presented as a route across biological barriers, including the blood-brain barrier

clinical_pipeline.unit: exosome clinical trials launched since 2022, as reported by WEF

observations.method: Report synthesis of scientific and commercial development examples; the clinical-trial count is retained as published context and not independently audited here.
observations.uncertainty: Technical progress does not establish clinical efficacy, affordability, safety, reimbursement, manufacturing capacity, or equitable access.
observations.subgroup: Patients, caregivers, clinicians, health systems, biomanufacturers, insurers, and people outside well-resourced sequencing and treatment systems.
observations.counterinterpretation: Personalization can improve fit and effectiveness while increasing data, manufacturing, regulatory, and affordability burdens and potentially widening health-system disparities.

trust_constraint.value: trust is described as a precondition for engineered food, personalized therapies, and household participation in distributed energy systems

access_constraint.value: the report warns that benefits may concentrate in regions and populations already positioned to capture them

governance_need.value: accountability, audit, assumption-testing, regulatory frameworks, standards, and compensation design are identified as necessary alongside technical progress

control_tradeoff.value: households may gain resilience or compensation from flexible energy assets while sharing data and giving up some control over charging and discharge

observations.method: Qualitative strategic outlook and emerging-landscape synthesis; no independent measurement of trust, access, or distributional outcomes.
observations.uncertainty: The report identifies plausible conditions and risks, but the direction and magnitude of public response, inequality, and institutional control remain open.
observations.subgroup: Households, renters, patients, agricultural communities, regulators, utilities, platform operators, and populations with limited capital or infrastructure access.
observations.counterinterpretation: Policy, public investment, open standards, and inclusive procurement could broaden access; unequal outcomes are risks in the report's default scenario, not fixed results.

related_sources.claim: Complementary sustainability-officer evidence on transition investment, adaptation, AI resource intensity, and resilience capital.
Complementary industrial evidence on circularity, resource security, repair, and recurring revenue.

boundary: This record adds a broad technology-and-society signal across distributed infrastructure, food production, health personalization, materials, household participation, trust, access, and governance. It is a foresight and expert-synthesis source, not a representative public-opinion measure, adoption forecast, clinical evaluation, causal impact estimate, or proof of equitable outcomes.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: Accessible official WEF digest and full-report emerging-landscape pages were reviewed for the ten-technology cohort, cross-cutting patterns, technology mechanisms, and trust/access conditions; the linked PDF endpoint timed out during retrieval.
